title: He Said Goodbye The Day We MET 📦
premise: On a sunny cul-de-sac, my new neighbor Vern, about 85, hugs me on my lawn the day I move in, cries, and thanks me for thirty years, because Vern lives his days in reverse: he gets younger every year I age, never remembers yesterday, only tomorrow, and his porch calendar counts down from 10,950.
twist: His last day on our street was my first, so thirty years later, on his first day, a young Vern moves in next door knowing nothing, and now I am the one who knows it all, cries, hugs him and thanks him for thirty years.
world: Two small houses side by side on a bright cul-de-sac: mine pale blue, Vern's butter yellow with a deep porch, a white picket fence between the yards, a maple that grows through the seasons, and a flip calendar on a nail by Vern's door.
